subject: EmberCommerce renewal: platform benchmark window, capacity & scaled terms
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@embercommerce.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@embercommerce.com>, Tom Benson <tbenson@embercommerce.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + competitive bench request

Marcus —

Hope you’re well. Our contract with Redwood comes up for renewal in early May and we’ve started a formal bakeoff. A competitor (ApexAI) reached out offering aggressive pricing and an accelerated migration play. Before we steer that way, Procurement wants a short, production-like benchmark so we can validate latency, throughput and per-token cost on our actual prompt mix.

Can Redwood run a 7–10 day benchmark in our staging environment mirroring our 95th percentile traffic (attached current utilization), and provide:
- end-to-end p95 latency numbers for the top 10 prompt types
- cost-per-1M tokens estimate at our observed distribution
- a clear path for guaranteed burst capacity if we need 2x traffic for 48 hrs

Also can you share a written offer for a 12 vs 24 month renewal (pricing + any onboarding/commitment credits) so Procurement has a baseline?

We’re on a tight cadence — the bakeoff kickoff is next Monday — so appreciate a quick confirmation on feasibility.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Ops | EmberCommerce
[Attachment: ember-current-utilization.csv]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@embercommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + competitive bench request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the utilization file. We can absolutely run a production-like benchmark and will/should mirror your 95th percentile distribution to make apples-to-apples comparisons. High level plan:

1) 10-day benchmark window in your staging (instrumented) with our devops to stream your workload subset. We’ll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and token accounting.
2) Dedicated bench pool option: we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool for the window to ensure isolation and deterministic results.
3) Pricing/terms: we’ll produce two offers (12m / 24m) with a one-time onboarding credit and a short-term burst commitment option (pre-paid burst blocks you can use inside 90 days).

Monica — can you draft the two-term pricing options and an indicative savings/commitment table? Rishi — can you draft the bench plan (I sketched a plan and attached it) and confirm the minimal access we’ll need to run in staging?

Alex — I attached a proposed benchmark plan PDF for quick review. If that looks fine we can aim to start the bench by Tuesday (2028-03-21).

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: redwood-proposed-benchmark-plan.pdf]
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@embercommerce.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-19T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + competitive bench request

Alex — looping in pricing details and a fast save offer. High level numbers below are indicative, final to be captured in a simple SOW:

Offer A (12 months):
- 12% list discount on hosted inference unit price
- One-time onboarding credit equal to 100k tokens (applied first invoice)
- 14-day dedicated benchmark window at no additional infra charge

Offer B (24 months):
- 18% list discount on hosted inference unit price
- Onboarding credit equal to 250k tokens
- 1 month (30 days) of free additional capacity (up to 20% of peak) to aid migration
- Priority dashed onboarding lane (3-business-day SLA for staging ops)

Burst blocks: pre-purchased 48-hr capacity blocks at a flat rate (we’ll include exact pricing in the attached spreadsheet).

If Procurement wants written confirmation of SOC2 and live audit artifacts, we can provide the SOC2 Type II summary plus an access window to our compliance portal. Tom — happy to coordinate with your procurement team on the legal timeline.

For transparency: these offers are contingent on a signed SOW within 30 days and a confirmed benchmark start date.

I attached the pricing workbook and a draft SOW; Marcus, please advise if we should sweeten the 24-month terms for a quick close.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing-summary-ember.xlsx] [Attachment: SOW-ember-extend-term-draft.pdf]
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@embercommerce.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@embercommerce.com>, Tom Benson <tbenson@embercommerce.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + competitive bench request

Thanks, Monica — these numbers look reasonable and give Procurement something tangible to evaluate. A few items to flag from our side:
- Procurement needs the draft SOW and a redlineable DocuSign link; can you provide a version we can send to legal?
- SOC2 artifacts look good but Procurement will request the auditor contact and the most recent report date.
- Our internal bakeoff kicks off Monday afternoon — we may ask you to join one session to review the benchmark instrumentation and initial telemetry.

Question: if we commit to 24 months today, can Redwood commit to a one-time migration credit that covers 50% of our engineering hours for migration (up to a capped amount)? That’s a major ask but would be the tie-breaker.

I’m looping Tom (procurement) to drive timing.

Alex

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: EmberCommerce renewal — finalize save package and enable bench

Team — quick internal thread to finalize what we send Ember tomorrow morning. Summary and asks:

What Ember asked: 7–10 day production-like benchmark in staging, SOC2 evidence, written 12/24m offers, and (ideally) a migration credit if they sign 24m.

Proposed external deliverables (send to Ember by 08:00 PDT 2028-03-22):
- Finalized SOW (redlineable DocuSign link) — Rishi to attach the Ops appendix and run legal through the migration credit cap. (Attachment: SOW-ember-extend-term-draft.pdf)
- Benchmark kickoff plan — Rishi to own instrumentation and a short runbook. (Attachment: redwood-proposed-benchmark-plan.pdf)
- Pricing spreadsheet (finalized) — Monica to confirm numbers in pricing-summary-ember.xlsx and authorize the 24m sweetener (additional 5% credit on onboarding or equivalent).
- Compliance evidence — Sean to pull SOC2 auditor contact and produce the summary page for procurement.

Approvals needed: Monica — please confirm: 24m total effective discount = 18% list + 5% onboarding sweetener (document as a capped migration credit line item). Rishi — confirm bench requirements and the earliest start (can we be live on Tue 3/21?). Sean — confirm SOC2 artifact availability and auditor point-of-contact.

If we greenlight the 24m sweetener, I’ll send Ember an updated DocuSign link and a one-page exec summary tying the commitment credit to SOW milestones.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
